    #!/bin/bash

    EOF
    chmod +x /tmp/probe/r.sh

- For multi-line YAML input use bash $'line1\nline2' quoting, or write the input to a file and use "$(cat f)".
- If a value starts with '-', argparse rejects it as an option; use the '--a=VALUE' form instead: /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a='-.inf'

- Run MANY cases (at least 60-120 distinct inputs for your domain). Batch them in loops so you use few tool calls.
- Save your full raw transcript to /tmp/probe/DOMAIN.txt (replace DOMAIN with your domain slug) so it can be grepped later.

YOUR OUTPUT: a dense, factual behavioral spec for your domain. Format as compact lines of
  input  =>  exit code + exact stdout (use \n for newlines, and mark trailing newlines/spaces explicitly)
plus a short "RULES INFERRED" section stating the precise rule (thresholds, formats, orderings).
Do NOT include shell boilerplate, do NOT narrate what you tried. Only findings. Be exhaustive but terse.
Where output has trailing '...' lines or blank lines, report them EXACTLY.

YOUR DOMAIN: how the emitter chooses a scalar STYLE and escapes characters (allow_unicode=True is set).
Use inputs of the form  k: "<double quoted escapes>"  to inject arbitrary characters into the loaded string, then observe how dump re-emits it.
Determine exactly when the output is: plain, 'single quoted', "double quoted", or a block scalar.
Cover:
- strings that would be re-resolved as another type: '123', 'true', 'null', '~', '2024-01-15', '.inf', '1:2', '', 'yes'

- embedded newlines: 'a\nb', 'a\n\nb', '\na', 'a\n', 'a\n\n', multiple lines
- tabs: '\t', 'a\tb', ' \t '
- control chars \x00 \x01 \x07 \x08 \x0b \x0c \x0d \x1b \x7f \x85 \xa0 \u2028 \u2029 \ufeff
- unicode: accents, CJK, emoji, combining marks
- backslashes, quotes: apostrophes, double quotes, both, 'a\\b'
- very long strings with and without spaces (test folding/wrapping at what column?)
- strings ending with ':' or ' ' or containing ': ' or ' #'
Report the exact output for each input, and a precise RULES section: the escape table (which chars become \0 \a \b \t \n \v \f \r \e \" \\ \N \_ \L \P \xXX \uXXXX \UXXXXXXXX), and the style-selection decision rules.

## RULES INFERRED

**Global.** Output = `yaml.dump(...)` (which ends in one LF) + `print`'s LF ⇒ every successful run ends with exactly two LF bytes. `default_flow_style` is the modern default (block output); flow input is re-emitted as block. `width` default ⇒ `best_width = 80`; `indent` default ⇒ `best_indent = 2`. Line break = LF.

**Only three styles ever appear: plain, `'single'`, `"double"`. Block scalars (`|`, `>`) are NEVER produced**, regardless of newline count, length, or trailing whitespace, because `yaml.dump` emits scalars with `style=None`.

**Style selection (block context; the emitter computes 4 booleans over the string):**
- `leading_space | leading_break | trailing_space | trailing_break` ⇒ not plain.
- `line_breaks` (contains LF, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029) ⇒ not plain.
- `break_space` (a break immediately followed by ' ') ⇒ not plain, not single-quoted.
- `space_break` (a ' ' immediately followed by a break) ⇒ not plain, not single-quoted.
- `special_characters` ⇒ not plain, not single-quoted. A char is special iff it is NOT `LF`, NOT `U+0020..U+007E`, NOT `U+0085`, NOT `U+00A0..U+D7FF`, NOT `U+E000..U+FFFD`, NOT `U+10000..U+10FFFE`, or IS `U+FEFF`. Hence TAB, all other C0, U+007F, U+0080..U+009F (≠U+0085), U+FEFF, surrogates, U+FFFE/U+FFFF, U+10FFFF are special.
- `block_indicators` ⇒ not plain. Set when: index 0 char ∈ `# , [ ] { } & * ! | > ' " % @ \``; or index 0 is `-`/`?`/`:` followed by space-or-end; or any interior `:` followed by space-or-end; or any interior `#` preceded by a space; or the string starts with `---` or `...`.
- empty string ⇒ not plain.
- The value would re-resolve to a non-str tag (int/float/bool/null/timestamp/merge `<<`/value `=`) ⇒ not plain (PyYAML's implicit resolvers; note `0o…`, `1e5`, `2.0e3`, `2024-1-5`, `y`/`n`/`Y`, `inf`/`nan`/`None`, `0:30` do **not** resolve, so they stay plain).
- Decision order: **plain** if allowed → else **`'single'`** if allowed → else **`"double"`**.

**Single-quoted specifics.** `'` → `''`. Each real line break becomes **two** LFs (a blank line) plus the indent; U+0085/U+2028/U+2029 are written as their own raw byte(s) as the "break", then the indent is appended (producing the `<char>  ` artifact). Single spaces fold as one LF + indent under the width rule.

**Double-quoted escape table (allow_unicode=True):**
`\0`=U+0000, `\a`=U+0007, `\b`=U+0008, `\t`=U+0009, `\n`=U+000A, `\v`=U+000B, `\f`=U+000C, `\r`=U+000D, `\e`=U+001B, `\"`=U+0022, `\\`=U+005C, `\N`=U+0085, `\L`=U+2028, `\P`=U+2029.
`\xXX` (UPPERCASE hex) for U+0001–U+0006, U+000E–U+001A, U+001C–U+001F, U+007F, U+0080–U+009F (except U+0085).
`\uXXXX` (UPPERCASE hex) for U+D800–U+DFFF, U+FFFE, U+FFFF, and U+FEFF.
`\UXXXXXXXX` for U+10FFFF only.
Everything else — including all of U+0020..U+007E except `"` and `\`, **U+00A0** (so `\_` is never emitted), and every printable non-ASCII up to U+10FFFE — is written raw UTF-8.

**Width/folding rules.**
- Plain & single-quoted: fold a space run only if `len(run)==1 && column_before_run > 80 && run not at either end`. Replacement: LF + `indent` spaces. Multi-space runs and space-free strings never fold.
- Double-quoted: fold when `column + len(pending_run) > 80` and (current char is `' '` or the pending run is empty, i.e. right after an escape) and the position is strictly interior (`0 < end < len-1`). Emits `\` + LF + `indent` spaces, then an extra `\` if the next char is `' '`.
- `indent` for a scalar = 2 × (its nesting depth), i.e. 2 at the top level of a mapping/sequence, 4 one level in, 6 two levels in.

**Document markers.** A root-level scalar emitted **plain** is followed by a `...` line (`OUT[<scalar>¶...¶¶]`); a root-level scalar emitted single- or double-quoted gets **no** `...`.

**Keys.** A key is emitted inline (`key: value`) only if its emitted scalar text is non-empty, single-line, and `len < 123`; otherwise the explicit form `? <key>¶: <value>` is used. (Threshold is `len(scalar) + len("!!str") < 128`.)
